customer_question: Our Bluetooth module reached EOL, so we're switching to a successor module with a different chip. We want to keep using our existing Declaration ID (DID/DN) -- what would this cost and what testing is actually needed?
question_variants: Do we need profile testing again if we switch to this successor module?
Does RF testing depend on whether the successor module has a built-in or external antenna?
Does the successor module's existing registration have any issues we should know about before we reference it?
actual_issue: The customer's product used a Bluetooth module that reached EOL and needed to be replaced with a successor module using a different chip, with the customer wanting to preserve continuity with the existing Declaration ID, and it needed to be determined what testing (profile and RF) was actually required for this transition, as well as whether the successor module's own registration carried any inherited issues.
plain_english_explanation: When swapping in a replacement Bluetooth module after the old one is discontinued, you don't necessarily need to redo all the testing from scratch. If the new module's own certification already covers the same features (profiles) the product currently supports, that part doesn't need retesting. Whether you need a radio test depends on how the new module handles its antenna -- modules with a built-in or plug-in antenna usually skip this, while one needing an external antenna typically doesn't. It's also worth knowing upfront if the new module's own certification record carries some old, leftover technical quirks from when it was first registered years ago -- these don't stop you from using it, but it's good to know they'll show up in your registration too.
consultant_answer: If the successor module D065231 (QDID referenced) is implemented, the profiles currently supported by the existing WX-PS200 registration are already included in that QDID, so profile testing is not required. Whether RF testing is needed depends on the successor module's antenna handling: (1) if the successor module has a built-in antenna or an antenna connector, the quote is for agency registration support (Single Design reference) and compliance folder preparation only, with a separate Qualification Fee wire transfer; (2) if the successor module is an external-antenna type, RF full-item testing is additionally required. Separately, the referenced D065231 QDID, when checked against the current registration site's Consistency Check rules (based on the current TCRL), shows several inter-layer consistency findings -- Mandatory dependency rules spanning BB, L2CAP, LL, and LMP, tied to HFP and GAP items -- carried forward from when this QDID was originally registered under the prior system. Even though these findings exist, the new registration is still permitted to proceed; there is no practical obstacle, but the customer's own new registration under their company name will also inherit this same module's inter-layer consistency findings, and they should be aware of this in advance.
decision_logic: For an EOL module replacement where registration continuity is desired, profile testing is unnecessary if the successor module's QDID already covers the existing product's supported profiles, and RF testing necessity is determined by the successor module's antenna configuration (built-in/connector antenna exempts it; external antenna requires it). An older module QDID's inherited inter-layer consistency findings from its original registration do not block a new registration referencing it, but should be disclosed to the customer in advance since the new registration will carry forward the same findings.
final_recommendation: When quoting an EOL module replacement with registration-continuity requirements, check the successor module's QDID against the existing product's supported profiles to scope profile testing, check its antenna configuration to scope RF testing, and proactively disclose any inherited inter-layer consistency findings from the successor module's original registration before the customer commits.
risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming full profile or RF testing is required without checking the successor module's QDID coverage and antenna configuration would lead to over-quoting. Failing to disclose inherited inter-layer consistency findings in advance could surprise the customer when the same findings appear in their own registration.
